display.purpose: Reserved for a full-width statement; no shipped view uses it yet.

headline.purpose: One per view: the view title, or the state word on the connect tile.

title.purpose: Dialog titles and the allowance figure.

readout.purpose: The exit IP and other values that are read rather than parsed; shrinks for long addresses.

body.purpose: Default running text and form values.

small.purpose: The workhorse: buttons, nav, setting labels, helper text.

caption.purpose: Setting descriptions, card labels, chips, log lines, error detail.

micro.purpose: Badges, timestamps, the title bar state line, hints.

mono.purpose: Machine strings only: IPs, hosts, ports, transports, bypass patterns, logs.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: A card at rest: contact shadow plus a wide, low pool. Felt, not seen.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Popovers, toasts, banners, tooltips — anything detached from the flow.

shadows.name: inner-top
shadows.purpose: 1 px top highlight on every raised surface in the dark theme; white inner line in the light theme.

shadows.name: orb-halo
shadows.purpose: The connected orb's halo: light pooled on the surface behind the core.

shadows.name: primary-underlight
shadows.purpose: The primary button's inner top edge and soft orange under-glow.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: View change, toast/banner entrance, focus ring settle.

motion.name: dur-4
motion.purpose: Modal entrance, disclosure and advanced-section expansion, nav pill slide.

motion.name: dur-5
motion.purpose: Orb settle, ring sweep, ambient state fade.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for anything entering or leaving.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Continuous loops: orb breathe, arc spin, dot pulse.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Nav pill, switch knob, segmented thumb, toast and modal entrance — nothing at rest.

motion.name: theme-reveal
motion.purpose: Circular clip-path reveal from the control that changed the theme.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action the screen exists for: orange fill, ink text, inner top edge and soft under-glow.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;height:36px;padding:0 14px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:10px;background:var(--accent,#FF7A3D);color:var(--accent-ink,#1A0C05);font-family:var(--font,"Segoe UI",system-ui,sans-serif);font-size:13px;font-weight:600;line-height:1;cursor:pointer;box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.18) inset,0 6px 18px rgba(255,122,61,.10);transition:background-color 140ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),transform 80ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)}.ds-btn-primary:hover{background:var(--accent-hover,#FF8A52)}.ds-btn-primary:active{background:var(--accent-press,#F06A2C);transform:translateY(1px)}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--text,#F5EFEB);outline-offset:2px;box-shadow:0 0 0 4px #000,0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.18) inset,0 6px 18px rgba(255,122,61,.10)}.ds-btn-primary[disabled]{opacity:.45;cursor:default}

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default for every action that is not the screen's purpose: ash fill, hairline edge, linen text.

components.name: Switch
components.description: A real role=switch button. White knob with a dark ink edge so the knob reads on the orange track; the knob stretches while held.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Ash fill with a deliberately visible 3:1 edge; focus turns the edge orange and lifts the fill.

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: State at chip weight: the label carries the tone, the ringed dot carries the transition.

components.name: Card
components.description: Dashboard card: ash surface, hairline border, ambient shadow, uppercase label and a mono value.

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Transport and mode picker: a thin-bordered trough with a white thumb that springs to the pressed option.
components.css: .ds-seg{position:relative;display:inline-flex;padding:3px;gap:2px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.34);border-radius:10px;background:var(--surface-2,#1E1A17);font-family:var(--font,"Segoe UI",system-ui,sans-serif)}.ds-seg-thumb{position:absolute;top:3px;bottom:3px;inset-inline-start:3px;width:52px;border-radius:6px;background:var(--surface-1,#161311);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.34);box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.18);pointer-events:none;transition:inset-inline-start 220ms var(--ease-spring,cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)),width 220ms var(--ease-spring,cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1))}.ds-seg button{position:relative;z-index:1;height:26px;padding-inline:12px;border:0;border-radius:6px;background:transparent;color:var(--text-2,#B8ABA3);font:inherit;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;transition:color 140ms}.ds-seg button:hover{color:var(--text,#F5EFEB)}.ds-seg button[aria-pressed="true"]{color:var(--text,#F5EFEB)}.ds-seg button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--text,#F5EFEB);outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Connected Orb (signature)
components.description: The connect tile's core: graphite lit from within, orange rim, halo behind it. Never a solid orange disc.
components.css: .ds-orb{position:relative;width:232px;height:232px;display:grid;place-items:center;cursor:pointer}.ds-orb-halo{position:absolute;inset:2%;border-radius:50%;background:radial-gradient(circle,rgba(255,122,61,.30) 0%,transparent 62%);filter:blur(22px)}.ds-orb-ring{position:absolute;inset:0;border-radius:50%;border:1px solid rgba(255,122,61,.5)}.ds-orb-core{position:relative;display:grid;place-items:center;width:150px;height:150px;border-radius:50%;background:radial-gradient(120% 120% at 34% 16%,rgba(255,154,102,.30) 0%,rgba(255,122,61,.10) 38%,transparent 68%),radial-gradient(120% 120% at 50% 120%,rgba(255,122,61,.16) 0%,transparent 60%),var(--surface-1,#161311);border:1px solid rgba(255,122,61,.55);color:var(--accent,#FF7A3D);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px rgba(255,122,61,.18) inset,0 0 44px rgba(255,122,61,.30),0 24px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.45);transition:transform 220ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1),box-shadow 700ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)}.ds-orb-core svg{filter:drop-shadow(0 0 10px rgba(255,122,61,.55))}.ds-orb:hover .ds-orb-core{transform:scale(.985)}

narrative.overview:
Ember is a dark-first Windows instrument with a warm graphite body and a single orange source that behaves like light. The default surface is coal; the panels above it are warm ash, not neutral grey, so the whole window sits in the same temperature as the fox-orange accent. Orange is almost absent when the tunnel is down and is the only light in the room when it is up: a glowing rim on the orb, a gradient arc on the allowance ring, a 2 px selected edge, one filled button.

The character is warm precision: a calm, dense, native Windows control panel that measures its contrast instead of trusting its eye, prefers a plain number to a reassuring sentence, and gives state its own vocabulary (idle, busy, ok, error) so the same four words mean the same thing in the title bar, the chip, the orb and the live region. Density is high — 13–14 px body text, 32–44 px controls, rows padded 13 px — because the person reading it is looking at a tunnel, not browsing a catalogue.

The material story is light in a dark room. Connected, the orb is graphite lit from within — a warm core, a bright rim, a halo on the surface behind it — rather than a solid orange disc. Green is scoped to the chip and never becomes the headline. Motion is tactile and quiet: 1 px press travel, a spring on the nav pill and the switch knob, a 360 ms spring only when a dialog actually arrives.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, with a light theme that is the same structure on warm paper — every component reads the same token names.
One accent, used as emitted light: rim, arc, glow, chip text, selected border, and exactly one primary button per screen.
Four warm surfaces in strict tonal steps; shadows only for things that float.
A 40 px drawn title bar and a 208 px rail that behave like Windows chrome, not like a website.
Native-density type: 11–14 px working text, four weights (400 body, 500 tooltip, 600 interface, 700 wordmark and counts), tabular numbers everywhere a value changes.
Full right-to-left layout for Persian, written with logical properties, with Latin values isolated.
Contrast measured against every surface a token can land on, in both themes, before the value ships.

rules.name: The Orange Is Light Rule
rules.body: Orange marks emitted state and selection. It may fill a button, a 2 px border, an arc, a dot, a glow, or a few words of text. It may never fill a card, a panel, a header, a row background at full strength, or more than roughly a tenth of any screen. If a screen looks orange, the screen is wrong.

rules.name: The Closed Palette Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the interface resolves to a token in web/css/tokens.css. A literal hex outside that file is a bug, and the two themes are two value sets behind one set of names, so no component knows which is active.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: A token ships only after its ratio is computed against every surface it can appear on, in both themes. Text is ≥ 4.5:1; the edge of a text field and a selected-state border are ≥ 3:1. Where the maths cannot reach the bar with a tint, the design changes shape.

rules.name: The Four Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 carries body and running text, 600 carries the interface (buttons, labels, titles, numbers), 700 belongs to the wordmark, avatars, log levels and account tiers, and 500 exists only for tooltip text. There is no light weight and no italic.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change while the window is open — a rate, a total, a countdown, an allowance, a port, an ID — is set in tabular numerals. Digits must not reflow the line on every poll.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: The mono face is a signal that the string is copied, pasted, compared or logged. A sentence is never mono; an IP, a hostname, a port, a transport or a log line always is.

rules.name: The Logical Properties Rule
rules.body: Layout is written in inline-start / inline-end / margin-inline / padding-inline throughout; the same CSS must produce the English and the Persian screen. Physical directions live only in web/css/direction.css.

rules.name: The Chrome Stays Still Rule
rules.body: The title bar and the rail are the window, not the page. They keep their own view-transition group and no animation, while only the content area fades or slides.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separating from its neighbour, step the surface colour or add a border. A shadow means the element floats, so a shadow on a row, a group, a setting or a header is a mistake, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Lit-Not-Painted Rule
rules.body: The connected orb is a graphite core lit from inside — warm radial highlight, orange rim, halo behind it. Never swap it for a solid orange disc: at this size that reads as an alarm.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: A shape has one radius. If a card is 14 px, its inner row is not also 14 px — it is either flush, or a 6–10 px control sitting inside it.

rules.name: The Drawn-Mark Rule
rules.body: The brand mark, the icon sprite and the window buttons are drawn in the same hand: 24 px grid, 1.75 stroke, round caps and joins, currentColor. Default Windows glyphs next to these make the chrome look like a browser window.

dos: Do put one orange action on a screen and let every other action be secondary, ghost or a link.
Do let state live in the chip, the dot and the orb, and keep the headline Linen unless the state is an error.
Do use the surface ladder (Coal → Ash 1 → Ash 2 → Ash 3) and 1 px borders to build hierarchy before reaching for a shadow.
Do set every changing number in tabular figures, and every machine string in mono with dir="ltr".
Do build controls from ui.js so they arrive with a role, a state, a name and a keyboard path.
Do verify contrast for both themes on the actual surface the element sits on — including the light theme's darker accent-text and success values.
Do write layout in logical properties and keep physical-direction exceptions in direction.css.
Do give Persian the same layout, not a narrower one: test the minimum window in both directions, since Persian labels are longer in places and shorter in others.
Do keep the title bar's order fixed — mark leading, window buttons trailing — in every language.
donts: Don't add a colour outside tokens.css, and don't add a value that only works in one theme.
Don't fill a card, panel, header or row background with full-strength orange, or let a screen read as orange overall.
Don't use a drop shadow on list rows, groups, settings rows or headers; those separate by tone and border.
Don't turn the connected orb into a solid orange disc, a 100 % progress bar, or a green success badge — the arc fades back to a quiet status ring for a reason.
Don't paint the connected headline green, or let green compete with the orange core.
Don't use 500, italics, or a second typeface to create hierarchy; size, weight and colour do that work.
Don't hide an affordance until hover — the copy button, the remove button and the favourite star stay visible or reachable by focus.
Don't place a banner over the content it is warning about; it belongs in the flow.
Don't animate continuously when nothing is happening, and never start an entrance from opacity: 0 on a view that may mount while the window is hidden.
Don't use Windows' default caption glyphs in the title bar; they are a different drawing system from the sprite.
